summary: First-order equation. 2 methods apply: Separation of variables and Integrating factor (linear).

methods.name: Separation of variables
methods.reason: The right-hand side factors as \(g(x)\,h(y)\) with \(g = x\) and \(h = y\).

steps.title: Recognise the form
steps.text: The equation is separable because the right-hand side is a function of \(x\) times a function of \(y\).

steps.title: Note the constant solutions
steps.text: Dividing by \(h(y)\) in the next step is only allowed where \(h(y) \neq 0\). Where \(h(y) = 0\) the slope is zero, so these constant functions are solutions on their own:

steps.title: Separate the variables
steps.text: Divide both sides by \(h(y)\) and multiply by \(dx\), so all the \(y\) terms are on the left and all the \(x\) terms are on the right.

steps.title: Integrate both sides
steps.text: Integrate the left side with respect to \(y\) and the right side with respect to \(x\). One constant of integration is enough.

steps.title: Solve for y
steps.text: Solve this equation for \(y\). An expression made only of the arbitrary constant, such as \(\pm e^{C}\) or \(2C\), is itself an arbitrary constant, so it is renamed \(C\).

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets the initial condition.

methods.verify_note: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets the initial condition.

methods.name: Integrating factor (linear)
methods.reason: It can be written as \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\) with \(p = - x\) and \(q = 0\).

steps.title: Write in standard form
steps.text: Move the \(y\) term to the left so the equation reads \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\).

steps.title: Find the integrating factor
steps.text: The integrating factor is \(\mu = e^{\int p\,dx}\).

steps.title: Multiply through by the integrating factor
steps.text: After multiplying by \(\mu\), the left side is exactly the derivative of the product \(\mu\,y\) (product rule in reverse).

steps.title: Integrate both sides
steps.text: The derivative of \(\mu\,y\) is zero, so \(\mu\,y\) is a constant.

steps.title: Solve for y
steps.text: Divide both sides by the integrating factor.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets the initial condition.

methods.verify_note: Checked symbolically by substituting back, and it meets the initial condition.

methods.name: Exact equation
methods.reason: Written as \(M\,dx + N\,dy = 0\), exactness needs \(\partial M/\partial y = \partial N/\partial x\). Here they are \(- x\) and \(0\), and the simpler methods above already apply.

methods.name: Bernoulli substitution
methods.reason: The equation does not have the form \(y' + p(x)\,y = q(x)\,y^n\) with \(n \ne 0, 1\).

methods.name: Homogeneous substitution (y = vx)
methods.reason: The right-hand side cannot be written as a function of \(y/x\) alone.

methods.name: Phase line (qualitative)
methods.reason: A phase line needs an autonomous equation \(y' = f(y)\); here the right-hand side depends on \(x\).
